comment: Human-maintained Parity Manifest classification rules (schema classification-rules-1.schema.json; semantics in ClassificationRules). Any entry in 'rules' beats any entry in 'defaults'; within a tier the most specific match wins (exact id > id glob with more literal characters > kind > deprecated); equally specific matches are an error. Defaults preserve only non-deprecated baseline entries and claim one dimension per kind; binary and behavioral claims need explicit rules backed by evidence. Deprecated entries have no default and must be classified explicitly.

rules.name: iam-policy-builder-api
rules.comment: Task 14.3. The V3 iam-policy-builder artifact keeps the whole V2 policy builder API. Source and binary claims: the generated compile, linkage, signature and hierarchy fixtures of codegen-generated-classes-test compatibility-scope.txt, and IamPolicyBuilderCompatibilityTest, which compares every public V2 member with V3 and runs V2-compiled caller bytecode against V3. Behavior claim: IamPolicyBuilderCompatibilityTest runs the released V2 library and V3 side by side on generated policies and documents (JSON text, accepted and rejected documents, exception types and messages, equality, hash and string rendering).
rules.rationale: V3 ports the V2 policy builder over public V3 core APIs with the same types, members, JVM descriptors and builder hierarchy, the same validation, equality, hash and string rendering, the same accepted documents and byte-identical JSON output.

rules.name: s3-event-notifications-api
rules.comment: Task 14.4. The V3 s3-event-notifications artifact keeps the whole V2 model API (same classes, constructors, accessors, setters, fromJson/toJson overloads, equals, hashCode and toString) and additionally implements SerializableStruct with a published SCHEMA per type. Source and binary claims: the generated compile, linkage, signature and hierarchy fixtures of codegen-generated-classes-test compatibility-scope.txt. The JSON reading and writing behavior is claimed by behavior:s3-event-notifications.model (launch-evidence-hooks.txt: S3EventNotificationV2DifferentialTest).
rules.rationale: The V3 event notification model types keep the V2 fully qualified names, members and JVM descriptors; they only add the SerializableStruct interface and SCHEMA/ID constants, so V2 source compiles and V2 bytecode links unchanged.

rules.name: dynamodb-enhanced-api
rules.comment: Tasks 14.1 and 14.6. The V3 dynamodb-enhanced artifact ports the whole V2 DynamoDB Enhanced Client public API over the public V3 DynamoDB and core APIs. Source claim: EnhancedV2ApiDescriptorParityTest compares every public and protected member of every non-internal V2 baseline type with V3 by name and JVM descriptor, the ported V2 unit suites of the module compile unchanged against V3, and the generated compile and source signature/hierarchy fixtures of codegen-generated-classes-test compatibility-scope.txt compile V2 callers of every entry against V3. Binary claim: the generated linkage and binary signature/hierarchy fixtures load V2-compiled caller bytecode of every entry against the V3 artifact (V2BytecodeOnV3Test, ApiShapeCompatibilityTest). Inherited V2 SdkPublisher operators are sdk-core entries (api:software.amazon.awssdk.core.async.SdkPublisher#*), not part of this claim. Behavior is claimed by the behavior:dynamodb-enhanced.* entries (launch-evidence-hooks.txt).
rules.rationale: The V3 enhanced client types keep the V2 fully qualified names, members, overloads and JVM descriptors, so V2 source that uses them compiles and V2 caller bytecode links unchanged.

rules.name: s3-transfer-manager-api
rules.comment: Task 14.6. The V3 s3-transfer-manager artifact keeps the V2 Transfer Manager public API over the public V3 S3 API; the more specific s3-transfer-manager-* rules are its ADAPTED members. Source and binary claims: the generated compile, linkage and signature/hierarchy fixtures of codegen-generated-classes-test compatibility-scope.txt (ManifestDiagnosticsTest, V2BytecodeOnV3Test, ApiShapeCompatibilityTest), which bind themselves to every entry they verify. The presigned-URL download API (downloadWithPresignedUrl, downloadFileWithPresignedUrl and the Presigned* model types) is not shipped: it is excluded from the fixture scope and stays NOT_SHIPPED in the launch gate. Behavior is claimed by the behavior:s3-transfer-manager.* entries (launch-evidence-hooks.txt).
rules.rationale: The V3 Transfer Manager types keep the V2 fully qualified names, members, overloads and JVM descriptors, so V2 source that uses them compiles and V2 caller bytecode links unchanged.

rules.name: s3-transfer-manager-upload-request-body
rules.comment: Task 14.6. Introduced by the V3 streaming-upload fix: the S3 client retries a request body only if it declares itself replayable (AsyncRequestBody.isReplayable()). The Transfer Manager sends the caller's body directly for a known-length upload below the multipart threshold; multipart parts are its own replayable bodies.
rules.rationale: requestBody keeps its V2 signature; a caller-supplied body is retried after its transmission began only when it declares itself replayable.
differences: A custom AsyncRequestBody that does not override isReplayable() (and AsyncRequestBody.fromPublisher) is sent once: when the single PutObject of an upload below the multipart threshold fails after transmission began, the upload fails with that failure instead of being retried by subscribing to the body again as V2 did. The AsyncRequestBody factory bodies (fromBytes, fromString, fromFile and the other from* methods) are replayable and retried as in V2.
rules.migration: Override isReplayable() to return true in a custom AsyncRequestBody whose subscribe() replays the same bytes on every subscription, or upload through an AsyncRequestBody factory body.

rules.name: legacy-retry-policy
rules.comment: V2 RetryPolicy and its builder are deprecated in favor of Modern Retry (Requirement 18).
rules.rationale: Legacy retry policies are replaced by the Modern Retry strategy API.
rules.migration: Replace the legacy retry policy with a Modern Retry strategy on the client builder.
rules.supportEvidence: V2 marks software.amazon.awssdk.core.retry.RetryPolicy @Deprecated in favor of RetryStrategy.

rules.name: legacy-request-signer-override
rules.comment: Pre-Smithy-Reference-Architecture signer overrides (Requirement 18.1).
rules.rationale: Pre-SRA signer APIs are excluded; signing is selected by auth scheme and identity provider.
rules.migration: Remove the legacy signer; configure the auth scheme and identity provider on the client builder.
rules.supportEvidence: Requirement 18.1: pre-Smithy-Reference-Architecture signer APIs are EXCLUDED from V3.

rules.name: legacy-signers-auth
rules.comment: Deprecated V2 auth signers (Aws4Signer, AwsS3V4Signer, BearerTokenSigner, signer params and execution attributes); the deprecated credentials APIs of the auth artifact are deprecated-credentials-api. The replacement is the Modern Auth signer contract (Requirement 18.7).
rules.rationale: Pre-Smithy-Reference-Architecture signer, presigner and signer-override APIs are excluded; signing is selected by auth scheme resolution (Requirements 18.1, 18.2).
rules.migration: Remove the legacy Signer/Presigner usage; configure the auth scheme, HttpSigner and identity provider on the client builder, or use the service presigner.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks these signer APIs @Deprecated in favor of software.amazon.awssdk.http.auth.spi.signer.HttpSigner.

rules.name: deprecated-credentials-api
rules.comment: Deprecated members of the V2 credentials providers (DefaultCredentialsProvider#create, ProcessCredentialsProvider.Builder#command(String)); not signer APIs, so not legacy-signers-auth.
rules.rationale: Deprecated V2 credentials API; V3 makes no preservation claim for it.
rules.migration: Use the non-deprecated replacement named in the V2 @deprecated Javadoc (for example DefaultCredentialsProvider.builder().build(), or ProcessCredentialsProvider.Builder#command(List)).
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks these credentials APIs @Deprecated.

rules.name: legacy-signers-core
rules.comment: Deprecated V2 core Signer, AsyncSigner and request-body signer contracts; the Presigner contract is legacy-presigner-core. The replacement is the Modern Auth signer contract (Requirement 18.7).
rules.rationale: Pre-Smithy-Reference-Architecture signer, presigner and signer-override APIs are excluded; signing is selected by auth scheme resolution (Requirements 18.1, 18.2).
rules.migration: Remove the legacy Signer/Presigner usage; configure the auth scheme, HttpSigner and identity provider on the client builder, or use the service presigner.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks these signer APIs @Deprecated in favor of software.amazon.awssdk.http.auth.spi.signer.HttpSigner.

rules.name: legacy-presigner-core
rules.comment: The deprecated V2 generic Presigner extension contract (Requirements 18.2, 18.3). Its replacement is the Modern Auth presigning adjustment that generated service presigners (for example S3Presigner) apply to the auth scheme option their client selects.
rules.rationale: The legacy Presigner extension contract is excluded; service presigners sign through the auth scheme their client's auth-scheme resolution selects (Requirements 18.2, 18.3).
rules.migration: Remove the legacy Presigner; presign with the service presigner (for example S3Presigner), which signs through the client's Modern Auth scheme.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks software.amazon.awssdk.core.signer.Presigner @Deprecated in favor of the service presigners and software.amazon.awssdk.http.auth.spi.signer.HttpSigner.

rules.name: legacy-signer-client-option
rules.comment: The deprecated V2 SIGNER and TOKEN_SIGNER advanced client options, client-level pre-SRA signer overrides (Requirement 18.1); the Modern Auth replacement is the modeled auth scheme options (Requirement 18.7).
rules.rationale: Pre-SRA signer APIs are excluded; signing is selected by auth scheme and identity provider.
rules.migration: Remove the signer advanced option; V3 signs each operation with the auth scheme its model selects, using the client's credentials or token identity provider.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks SdkAdvancedClientOption.SIGNER and TOKEN_SIGNER @Deprecated in favor of auth schemes.

rules.name: legacy-signer-override-utils
rules.comment: Deprecated V2 signer-override helpers. The replacement is the modeled auth scheme options of the Modern Auth scheme resolution (Requirement 18.7).
rules.rationale: Pre-Smithy-Reference-Architecture signer, presigner and signer-override APIs are excluded; signing is selected by auth scheme resolution (Requirements 18.1, 18.2).
rules.migration: Remove the legacy Signer/Presigner usage; configure the auth scheme, HttpSigner and identity provider on the client builder, or use the service presigner.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks these signer APIs @Deprecated in favor of software.amazon.awssdk.http.auth.spi.signer.HttpSigner.

rules.name: legacy-retry-core
rules.comment: Deprecated V2 retry backoff strategies, retry conditions and retry-policy helpers (Requirement 18.4).
rules.rationale: Legacy retry policies, backoff strategies and retry conditions are excluded in favor of Modern Retry strategies (Requirement 18.4).
rules.migration: Replace the legacy backoff strategy or retry condition with a Modern Retry strategy configured on the client builder.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks these retry APIs @Deprecated in favor of software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api.RetryStrategy.

rules.name: legacy-retry-policy-client-override
rules.comment: The deprecated V2 retry-policy setters of the client override configuration (Requirement 18.4); the Modern Retry replacement is the strategy the V3 client builder accepts (Requirement 18.8).
rules.rationale: Legacy retry policies are replaced by the Modern Retry strategy API.
rules.migration: Configure a Modern Retry strategy with retryStrategy on the client builder (for retry mode standard or adaptive, StandardRetryStrategy or AdaptiveRetryStrategy) instead of the override configuration's retry policy.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks ClientOverrideConfiguration.Builder#retryPolicy @Deprecated in favor of retryStrategy.

rules.name: client-override-retry-strategy
rules.comment: Task 15.5 (Migration Corpus, retry-override): the non-deprecated V2 retry-strategy members of the client override configuration (the retryStrategy setters and getters and retryStrategyConfigurator). The V3 ClientOverrideConfiguration has no retry settings; every V3 client builder takes the Modern Retry strategy itself (retryStrategy(software.amazon.awssdk.retries.RetryStrategy)), so these members are not preserved and the move is a manual one.
rules.rationale: V3 configures the Modern Retry strategy on the client builder, not on the client override configuration.
differences: The V3 ClientOverrideConfiguration and its builder have no retryStrategy members; the V3 client builder's retryStrategy(RetryStrategy) takes a software.amazon.awssdk.retries.RetryStrategy (the V3 package of the Modern Retry SPI).
V3 has no RetryMode or Consumer<RetryStrategy.Builder> overload on the client builder: build StandardRetryStrategy or AdaptiveRetryStrategy explicitly.
rules.migration: Call retryStrategy(strategy) on the client builder instead of the override configuration, with a software.amazon.awssdk.retries.RetryStrategy (for retry mode standard or adaptive, StandardRetryStrategy or AdaptiveRetryStrategy).

rules.name: legacy-retry-backoff
rules.comment: Deprecated V2 legacy backoff strategies (Requirement 18.4); the Modern Retry replacement is its backoff contract (Requirement 18.8).
rules.rationale: Legacy retry policies, backoff strategies and retry conditions are excluded in favor of Modern Retry strategies (Requirement 18.4).
rules.migration: Replace the legacy backoff strategy with a Modern Retry BackoffStrategy (none, fixedDelay or exponentialDelay) on the Modern Retry strategy builder.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks these backoff strategies @Deprecated in favor of software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api.BackoffStrategy.

rules.name: legacy-retry-conditions
rules.comment: Deprecated V2 legacy retry conditions (Requirement 18.4); the Modern Retry replacement is its retry classifier contract (Requirement 18.8).
rules.rationale: Legacy retry policies, backoff strategies and retry conditions are excluded in favor of Modern Retry strategies (Requirement 18.4).
rules.migration: Replace the legacy retry condition with a Modern Retry RetryClassifier, or retryOnException, on the Modern Retry strategy builder.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks these retry conditions @Deprecated in favor of software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api.RetryStrategy.

rules.name: legacy-retry-strategy
rules.comment: The V2 legacy-mode retry strategy (Requirement 18.4; design 'Migration API comparison': legacy retry policy and legacy strategy are EXCLUDED). V3's Modern Retry modes are standard and adaptive only (software.amazon.awssdk.retries.RetryMode). Not deprecated in V2, so the general-availability gate reports it until the exclusion is approved.
rules.rationale: The pre-Smithy-Reference-Architecture legacy retry mode is excluded; V3 retries with the standard or adaptive Modern Retry strategy (Requirement 18.4).
rules.migration: Replace the legacy retry strategy with StandardRetryStrategy (retry mode standard) on the client builder; review its different default attempts and backoff.
rules.supportEvidence: Requirement 18.4 and the design's Migration API comparison exclude the legacy retry strategy; V3 RetryMode has no legacy mode.

rules.name: legacy-retry-strategy-default-builder
rules.comment: DefaultRetryStrategy#legacyStrategyBuilder (see legacy-retry-strategy).
rules.rationale: The pre-Smithy-Reference-Architecture legacy retry mode is excluded; V3 retries with the standard or adaptive Modern Retry strategy (Requirement 18.4).
rules.migration: Replace the legacy retry strategy with StandardRetryStrategy (retry mode standard) on the client builder; review its different default attempts and backoff.
rules.supportEvidence: Requirement 18.4 and the design's Migration API comparison exclude the legacy retry strategy; V3 RetryMode has no legacy mode.

rules.name: legacy-retry-aws
rules.comment: Deprecated V2 AWS retry-policy helpers (AwsRetryPolicy) (Requirement 18.4).
rules.rationale: Legacy AWS retry policies are excluded in favor of Modern Retry strategies (Requirement 18.4).
rules.migration: Replace AwsRetryPolicy with a Modern Retry strategy configured on the client builder.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks AwsRetryPolicy @Deprecated in favor of software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api.RetryStrategy.

rules.name: modern-retry-spi-artifact
rules.comment: Task 15.5 (Migration Corpus, modern-types-registry): the V2 Modern Retry SPI artifact. Its types (software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api) are the modern-retry-* entries, whose V3 types ship in the V3 retries artifact; V3 builds no retries-spi artifact, so a dependency on it moves to retries, which the dependency recipes rewrite.
rules.rationale: V3 ships the Modern Retry SPI in its retries module, under the V3 package software.amazon.awssdk.retries.
differences: V3 has no retries-spi artifact: the Modern Retry SPI types move from software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api in retries-spi to software.amazon.awssdk.retries in retries (see the modern-retry-* entries).
rules.migration: Depend on software.amazon.awssdk:retries instead; the migration tool rewrites the dependency coordinates.

rules.name: modern-auth-spi-artifact
rules.comment: Task 15.5 (Migration Corpus, modern-types-registry): the V2 Modern Auth SPI artifact. Its types (software.amazon.awssdk.http.auth.spi) are the modern-auth-* entries, whose V3 types ship in the V3 auth-api artifact; V3 builds no http-auth-spi artifact, so a dependency on it moves to auth-api, which the dependency recipes rewrite.
rules.rationale: V3 ships the Modern Auth SPI in its auth-api module, under the V3 package software.amazon.awssdk.auth.api.
differences: V3 has no http-auth-spi artifact: the Modern Auth SPI types move from software.amazon.awssdk.http.auth.spi in http-auth-spi to software.amazon.awssdk.auth.api in auth-api (see the modern-auth-* entries).
rules.migration: Depend on software.amazon.awssdk:auth-api instead; the migration tool rewrites the dependency coordinates.

rules.name: interceptor-execution-interceptor
rules.comment: Task 15.5 (Migration Corpus, audit-interceptor): the non-deprecated V2 ExecutionInterceptor and its hooks. V3 does not ship software.amazon.awssdk.core.interceptor; its interceptor contract is software.amazon.awssdk.pipeline.ExecutionInterceptor, whose hooks take one typed HookContext and follow the V3 lifecycle (design "Interceptor migration rules"). Hook conversions need the lifecycle review that design describes, so the migration is a located diagnostic.
rules.rationale: V3 replaces the V2 interceptor contract with the V3 pipeline interceptor: same role, typed hook contexts, V3 lifecycle.
differences: V3 hooks take a single software.amazon.awssdk.pipeline.HookContext subtype and no ExecutionAttributes; execution attributes become typed ContextKey values of the execution context.

modifyHttpRequest maps to modifyBeforeSigning, which runs once per attempt with the resolved endpoint visible; modifyRequest returns a SerializableStruct; modifyException keeps the terminal execution scope and per-attempt exceptions have modifyAttemptException.
Interceptors are registered with addExecutionInterceptor on the V3 client builder, not on the client override configuration.
rules.migration: Implement software.amazon.awssdk.pipeline.ExecutionInterceptor: move each hook to its V3 hook (modifyHttpRequest to modifyBeforeSigning), read its values from the HookContext and the typed execution context, check that it is safe at the V3 hook's lifecycle point and frequency, and register it with addExecutionInterceptor on the client builder.

rules.name: interceptor-execution-interceptor-hooks
rules.comment: The hooks and other members of the V2 ExecutionInterceptor (see interceptor-execution-interceptor).
rules.rationale: V3 replaces the V2 interceptor contract with the V3 pipeline interceptor: same role, typed hook contexts, V3 lifecycle.
differences: V3 hooks take a single software.amazon.awssdk.pipeline.HookContext subtype and no ExecutionAttributes; execution attributes become typed ContextKey values of the execution context.

modifyHttpRequest maps to modifyBeforeSigning, which runs once per attempt with the resolved endpoint visible; modifyRequest returns a SerializableStruct; modifyException keeps the terminal execution scope and per-attempt exceptions have modifyAttemptException.
Interceptors are registered with addExecutionInterceptor on the V3 client builder, not on the client override configuration.
rules.migration: Implement software.amazon.awssdk.pipeline.ExecutionInterceptor: move each hook to its V3 hook (modifyHttpRequest to modifyBeforeSigning), read its values from the HookContext and the typed execution context, check that it is safe at the V3 hook's lifecycle point and frequency, and register it with addExecutionInterceptor on the client builder.

rules.name: interceptor-context
rules.comment: Task 15.5: the non-deprecated V2 interceptor hook contexts (software.amazon.awssdk.core.interceptor.Context and its nested Context.* types). V3 replaces them with the sealed software.amazon.awssdk.pipeline.HookContext hierarchy.
rules.rationale: V3 replaces the V2 interceptor contexts with typed V3 hook contexts.
differences: The V3 HookContext subtypes follow the V3 hooks (for example ModifyBeforeSigning instead of ModifyHttpRequest), expose the request as a SerializableStruct and the operation, options and execution context, and add attempt contexts for per-attempt hooks.
rules.migration: Use the HookContext subtype of the V3 hook the interceptor moves to and read the request, HTTP request or response from it.

rules.name: interceptor-execution-attributes
rules.comment: Task 15.5: the non-deprecated V2 execution attribute types (ExecutionAttribute, ExecutionAttributes and their builders) and their members. V3 replaces untyped execution attributes with typed ContextKey values of the execution and attempt contexts (design "Interceptor migration rules").
rules.rationale: V3 replaces execution attributes with typed context keys.
differences: V3 stores per-call and per-attempt values under typed software.amazon.awssdk.core.context.ContextKey keys of the execution and attempt contexts; the SDK's own values (operation, endpoint, auth scheme, identity, attempt number) are HookContext accessors and PipelineKeys keys. Unknown V2 keys have no automatic mapping.
rules.migration: Declare a ContextKey for each application attribute and read the SDK's values from the HookContext (for example operation()) or PipelineKeys.

rules.name: interceptor-sdk-execution-attributes
rules.comment: Task 15.5: the non-deprecated execution attribute keys of the V2 SDK (SdkExecutionAttribute; see interceptor-execution-attributes). The V3 values they carried are HookContext accessors and PipelineKeys keys.
rules.rationale: V3 replaces execution attributes with typed context keys.
differences: V3 stores per-call and per-attempt values under typed software.amazon.awssdk.core.context.ContextKey keys of the execution and attempt contexts; the SDK's own values (operation, endpoint, auth scheme, identity, attempt number) are HookContext accessors and PipelineKeys keys. Unknown V2 keys have no automatic mapping.
rules.migration: Declare a ContextKey for each application attribute and read the SDK's values from the HookContext (for example operation()) or PipelineKeys.

rules.name: modern-retry-retry-strategy
rules.comment: Task 15.4: the V2 Modern Retry type software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api.RetryStrategy keeps its name in the V3 package of software.amazon.awssdk.retries.RetryStrategy; the retry.modern-type-package migration recipe rewrites its imports and qualified references. Its members are modern-retry-retry-strategy-members.
rules.rationale: The Modern Retry SPI is a V3 core module with V3 packages; the type keeps its name and role.
differences: V3 moves the Modern Retry SPI from software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api to software.amazon.awssdk.retries: a strategy refreshes a token with the failed attempt (AttemptFailure) and returns a RetryDecision instead of exchanging RefreshRetryTokenRequest/Response and RecordSuccessRequest/Response objects.
rules.migration: Import software.amazon.awssdk.retries.RetryStrategy instead; the migration tool rewrites single-type imports and fully qualified references.

rules.comment: The members of the V2 Modern Retry type software.amazon.awssdk.retries.api.RetryStrategy.Builder (see modern-retry-retry-strategy-builder).
rules.rationale: The Modern Retry SPI is a V3 core module with V3 packages; member signatures follow the V3 contract.

rules.name: sns-message-manager-api
rules.comment: Task 14.5. The V3 sns-message-manager keeps the V2 public types, members and JVM descriptors (SdkBytes, Region and ToString keep their V2 names in V3); exceptions are the more specific sns-message-manager-* rules. Verified by the generated compatibility fixtures (codegen-generated-classes-test compatibility-scope.txt).
rules.rationale: The V3 SNS Message Manager keeps the V2 public API with identical JVM descriptors, so V2 sources compile and V2 caller bytecode links against it.

rules.name: sns-message-manager-parse-message
rules.comment: Task 14.5. Parsing and signature verification run end to end against the V3 library with locally generated test certificates (no network).
rules.rationale: parseMessage keeps its V2 overloads and returns the same typed, signature-verified messages, rejecting unsigned, tampered and foreign-certificate messages with SdkClientException.

rules.name: sns-message-manager-builder-http-client
rules.comment: Task 14.5. The V2 SdkHttpClient is the V3 SdkSyncHttpClient (HTTP SPI, Requirement 12.1).
rules.rationale: The builder takes the certificate-retrieval client as the V3 sync HTTP SPI type; ownership is unchanged (a caller-supplied client is never closed by the manager).
differences: Takes software.amazon.awssdk.http.SdkSyncHttpClient instead of software.amazon.awssdk.http.SdkHttpClient; V2 HTTP clients cannot be passed.
rules.migration: Pass a V3 SdkSyncHttpClient (for example the V3 apache-client, apache5-client or url-connection-client), or omit httpClient to use the installed V3 HTTP implementation.

rules.name: sns-message-manager-subscription-confirmation-to-string
rules.comment: Task 14.5; Requirement 21.10. A subscription token confirms the subscription by itself.
rules.rationale: toString keeps its signature and format but redacts the subscription token.
differences: The Token field, and the Token query parameter of SubscribeUrl, render as '*** Sensitive Data Redacted ***' instead of their values.
rules.migration: Read token() and subscribeUrl() instead of parsing toString().

rules.name: sns-message-manager-unsubscribe-confirmation-to-string
rules.comment: Task 14.5; Requirement 21.10. The token re-confirms the subscription by itself.
rules.rationale: toString keeps its signature and format but redacts the subscription token.
differences: The Token field, and the Token query parameter of SubscribeUrl, render as '*** Sensitive Data Redacted ***' instead of their values.
rules.migration: Read token() and subscribeUrl() instead of parsing toString().

rules.name: sns-message-manager-verification-behavior
rules.comment: Task 14.5; Requirements 16.8, 21.10. Declared by the V3 artifact in META-INF/aws-sdk-java-v3/parity/capabilities.txt.
rules.rationale: SNS message parsing, certificate URL and signing-name validation, certificate caching and signature verification keep the V2 rules and V2 diagnostics; failure diagnostics no longer carry message content.
differences: A message body that is not well-formed JSON is rejected with SdkClientException carrying no cause, instead of the UncheckedIOException of the V2 JSON parser.

A message URL that cannot be parsed is rejected with SdkClientException('Unable to parse URI') without the V2 IllegalArgumentException cause, whose message quoted the URL (a SubscribeURL carries the subscription token).
Nothing is logged; V2 logged the canonical signed string (message body and subscription token) and the resolved certificate endpoint at DEBUG.

Without httpClient, build() selects the installed V3 sync HTTP implementation (connection timeout 10s, read timeout 30s, as in V2) and fails with HttpImplementationSelectionException when none is installed.
rules.migration: Catch SdkClientException for every rejected message; add a V3 HTTP implementation dependency (or pass httpClient) where V2 relied on a V2 HTTP implementation on the class path.

rules.name: deprecated-runtime-http
rules.comment: Remaining deprecated http-client-spi and HTTP Implementations APIs under software.amazon.awssdk.http not covered by a more specific legacy-* rule. Deprecated entries do not gate GA (Requirement 16.15); reclassify an entry as PRESERVED when candidate evidence shows V3 keeps it.
rules.rationale: Deprecated V2 runtime API; V3 makes no preservation claim for it.
rules.migration: Use the non-deprecated replacement named in the V2 @deprecated Javadoc.
rules.supportEvidence: The V2 baseline marks this API, or its declaring type, @Deprecated.

rules.name: s3-transfer-manager-completed-object-transfer-response
rules.comment: Task 14.2. V3 has no SdkResponse base type: generated responses implement the Smithy Java SerializableStruct.
rules.rationale: CompletedObjectTransfer.response() keeps its name and meaning but returns the V3 response supertype.
differences: Returns software.amazon.smithy.java.core.schema.SerializableStruct instead of software.amazon.awssdk.core.SdkResponse; the concrete completed-transfer types still return their typed S3 response.
rules.migration: Declare the result as SerializableStruct, or use the typed response() of CompletedFileUpload, CompletedUpload, CompletedFileDownload or CompletedCopy.

rules.name: s3-transfer-manager-progress-snapshot-sdk-response
rules.comment: Task 14.2. Same JVM descriptor (Optional is erased), so V2 bytecode links and erased V2 source compiles (task 14.6: the generated linkage and compile fixtures verify both); the element type changes from SdkResponse to SerializableStruct.
rules.rationale: TransferProgressSnapshot.sdkResponse() keeps its name and descriptor; its element type is the V3 response supertype.
differences: Returns Optional<software.amazon.smithy.java.core.schema.SerializableStruct> instead of Optional<software.amazon.awssdk.core.SdkResponse>.
rules.migration: Declare the element type as SerializableStruct (or cast to the typed S3 response).
